description: Quality documents (directive P8): the paper assembly order (AO) packets QA/QC files in SharePoint (QCQA '2026 - AOs'), read by the document-field extractor (ontology/document_fields.py, class ao_packet; scans from the capture's OCR text) into AssemblyOrderPacket objects. Every value is a page/span-cited machine-read lead. Planned, produced, filled, retained, inspected, released, rejected and damaged quantities keep their own roles and are never interchanged; damage stays per component; a blank paper field is unknown, never zero. The packet links to the AssemblyOrder, SalesOrder and bulk Batch it names (lead mentions); plx.object compares its fields with the FM values and reports each disagreement as a conflict (the attests rules of document_fields.json), never a pick. Vendor certificates of analysis (class certificate_of_analysis, mail attachments and the Portal's Receiving/Raw/{supplier}/{rawcode} SharePoint files) project into CertificateOfAnalysis objects: product, lot, dates, supplier and the test table as written, a lead linked to the PurchaseOrder it names, never a QC release. Field meanings mirror Portal ManufacturingOrder / AssemblyOrderDamage (plx-customer-portal portal/prisma/schema.prisma@8e3a951).

object_types.description: A paper AO packet (AO form, shop-floor sheet, finished-goods inspection / release sheet) projected from captured SharePoint files the document-field extractor recognises (class ao_packet): lots, dates, role quantities and per-component damage, each a machine-read lead cited to the original bytes (page and span; a scan's OCR text by its own SHA-256). Linked to its AssemblyOrder by the AO number it names; never merged with it.

bindings.note: One object per captured SharePoint file version recognised as class ao_packet (ontology/schema/document_fields.json); keyed by the source record, cited by its byte-pinned handle, same audience and validity interval as the source version.

object_types.description: A supplier's certificate of analysis (CoA) of one lot of a material, projected from captured mail attachments and SharePoint files (the Portal files vendor CoAs under Receiving/Raw/{supplier}/{rawcode}, devloop/CONTEXT/03-PORTAL.md) that the document-field extractor recognises (ontology/document_fields.py, class certificate_of_analysis): product, lot, manufacture and expiry dates, supplier, and the test table (test, specification, result, unit, method per line, in evidence.line_items), each a machine-read lead cited to the original bytes by page and span; a blank or unreadable cell is that cell's gap. A supplier's statement: never a QC release, a verified result or proof that a receipt is this lot.

link_types.name: for_receipt_line
link_types.description: A certificate of analysis states the supplier lot this ReceiptLine received: its lot field's value as the lot_number normaliser reads it, resolved only on ReceiptLine.supplier_lot_number in the identifier index (ontology/document_fields.py store_document_links, refers_to_property), never through a PLX lab id or batch code (a supplier lot is not a PLX lot: devloop/DECISIONS/2026-10-20-documents-lot-trace-supplier-lot.md). The lot trace runs on from the line: ReceiptLine.line_of -> Receipt.supplied_by -> Supplier, ReceiptLine.receives_line -> PurchaseOrderLine.line_of -> PurchaseOrder (or Receipt.receives), ReceiptLine.for_item -> Product. Always a lead: several lines received the same supplier lot stay several links, and the document's author is unknown (an external assertion).
